run_metadata.seed_myth:
Myth: Before courage existed, there were two weavers—Spinner of Thread and Holder of Loom. They had reconciled after discovering wind had stolen their cloth, not each other's betrayal.

"Shall we weave again?" they asked together.

But when Spinner brought new threads, they tangled immediately. When Holder tried the loom, the shuttle jammed. Nothing worked as it once had.

"Perhaps the wind has cursed us," Spinner said, stepping back.

Holder's shoulders sagged. "Or perhaps we've forgotten how to trust our own hands."

They sat beside the silent loom as darkness gathered. Then Holder spoke quietly: "We learned the wind deceived us. But now fear deceives us more completely."

Spinner picked up a single thread. "One thread, then. Just to begin."

Holder guided it through. It held.

They added another thread. Then another. Their rhythm returned slowly—not from certainty, but from choosing motion over stillness.

When morning came, they had woven something small but whole.

They learned that reconciliation isn't a single moment of forgiveness—it's the daily choice to place thread after thread, even when hands tremble. The loom doesn't care why we stopped. It only responds when we begin again.
